key: Step-up in basis: the gains tax is gone
lead: Gains never taxed. Loan repaid. The rest is theirs.
detail: At death, heirs inherit at a stepped-up basis. The estate repays the $5.5M loan from the top; $13.5M passes on.
note: Illustrative numbers · a typical path, not a forecast
svgLabel: Illustrative 30-year plan. A $2.5M portfolio grows to $19.0M while a credit line pays the living costs. Moving from St. Louis to Bangkok cuts the yearly draw from $80K to $47K, so the loan ends at $5.5M instead of $9.4M, below the margin-call line, and the odds the plan holds rise from 63% to 93%. At death the gains tax is wiped out by the step-up in basis, the estate repays the loan, and heirs keep $13.5M.
stepsLabel: How it works, step through the four beats

steps.name: 01 Buy
steps.body: Hold assets that grow. Never sell them, so the gains are never taxed.

steps.name: 02 Borrow
steps.body: Live on a line of credit secured by the portfolio. The loan grows; so, usually, do the shares.

steps.name: 03 Live anywhere
steps.body: Spend the loan where life costs less. A smaller loan gives the portfolio an easier race to win.

steps.name: 04 Die
steps.body: Heirs inherit at a stepped-up basis. The estate repays the loan and keeps the rest.
